params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The round grey cartoon creature with the big pointed ears and the wide friendly grin hoists the heavy sledgehammer high over its head, coils its whole body back, and whips the hammer into the broken edge of the hole in the wall in a hard smear. A burst of plaster chunks and wood splinters flies out of the wall and clatters down onto the rubble. It hops back on the spot, delighted, drops the hammer's head to the floor, slaps the side of the cardboard rocket with its free hand and leans an elbow on it, admiring the nose cone. Then it hoists the hammer overhead, coils back even harder, and whips it into the wall again, and another burst of plaster clatters down.

Its face is exactly two red-orange eyes and one wide grin of small teeth, the same two eyes and the same grin in every frame. Its two tall pointed ears are the same two ears in every frame. It lands on both feet on the floor after every hop. It stays small, no taller than a third of the tall shelving of binders at frame right, in every frame. The cardboard rocket stays leaning in the same place at the same angle in every frame. Through the hole there is only blank cream paper in every frame. The dartboard, the overturned side table, the stacked crates, the storage bench and the shelving stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
